title: CARS Act Total-Payable Disclosure — CA-CARS-003
quote: Monthly payment advertised on specials without the total amount payable over the term.
statute: Cal. Civ. Code §1784.41(c)(1) (CARS Act, SB 766) | CALIFORNIA controls: CARS Act (SB 766, Cal. Civ. Code §1784.20 et seq.), operative Oct 1, 2026. The federal FTC CARS Rule (16 CFR Part 463) was VACATED by the 5th Circuit (Jan 2025) and formally WITHDRAWN from the CFR (Fed. Reg. Feb 2026) — not enforceable. Subsection pin-cites verified against the chaptered statute (leginfo) 2026-06-28.
recommendation: California's CARS-style requirement is not operative until Oct 1, 2026 — fix now to be ready. This is a CALIFORNIA requirement, not a federal one. Under the CARS Act (operative Oct 1, 2026) any monthly-payment ad must also disclose the total the consumer will have paid after all scheduled payments.

title: Lease 'due at signing' headline contradicts the actual due-at-signing amount in the same disclaimer
quote: LEASE FOR $229 per month ... and $2495 due at signing. ... (Includes due at signing of $1999 plus tax title license fees and dmv fees & first month payment.)
statute: CA B&P Code 17501 / VC 11713.1; Reg M (12 CFR 1013)
recommendation: Every lease offer on the Specials page advertises a uniform '$2495 due at signing' in the headline, but each disclaimer's parenthetical states a different actual due-at-signing figure: Altima $1999, Sentra $4995, Rogue $5495, Kicks $4995, Pathfinder $2995, Murano $4495, Frontier $5995. A consumer reading the prominent '$2495' would be misled about the true upfront cost on six of seven vehicles. Reconcile the headline due-at-signing amount with the actual amount in each disclaimer so they match exactly, and ensure the controlling figure is the one shown prominently.

title: Material lease terms collapsed behind '[ +DISCLAIMER ]' expand toggles

Specials

2026 Nissan Altima SV - 1 at this price
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — The automated audit cannot assess font size, contrast, or whether the expand toggle is reasonably noticeable, and the qualifying lease terms (term length, mileage, residual, due-at-signing, fees) sit behind a click-to-expand '[ +DISCLAIMER ]' control rather than appearing with the payment claim. Manually verify that the disclaimer toggle is conspicuous near each advertised payment and that the expanded text is readable at normal viewing size on desktop and mobile. If a reasonable consumer would not notice or open the toggle, the disclosures are not clear and conspicuous.

title: 'Total Savings' claimed against an unsubstantiated 'Retail Price' on a used vehicle
quote: Retail Price $26,560 ... Dealer Discount -$3,569 ... Total Savings $3,569 ... Total Price $23,076
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — Could not verify whether the stated 'Retail Price' represents a genuine prior or prevailing price for this specific used unit. On used vehicles, a 'Total Savings' figure must reference a bona fide prior selling price, not an arbitrary inflated 'retail' number. Verify that $26,560 is a defensible reference price (e.g., documented prior listing or recognized guide value) for VIN JN1BF0AA2RM433701; if it is not substantiable, the $3,569 'savings' claim should be removed or relabeled.

title: 'Total Savings' claimed against an unsubstantiated 'Retail Price' on a used vehicle
quote: Retail Price $26,495 ... Dealer Discount -$3,704 ... Total Savings $3,704 ... Total Price $22,876
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — Could not verify whether the 'Retail Price' of $26,495 reflects a genuine prior or prevailing price for this specific used unit (VIN 2C3CDXHG7MH616604). title: Net price includes stacked manufacturer cash with qualifications not shown at the price
quote: Dealer Discount -$650 ... Nissan WR All Markets - MY26 Sentra (SV SR) Customer Cash - June -$500 ... Nissan Customer Cash -$500 ... Total Savings $1,650 ... Net Price $23,710
recommendation: The advertised Net Price of $23,710 stacks a dealer discount plus two separate Nissan Customer Cash incentives ($500 + $500). The page does not state, at the price, whether both manufacturer cash offers can be combined by the same buyer or whether either is conditional. Confirm both incentives are genuinely combinable and applicable to all buyers; if either is conditional (e.g., region, finance-contingent), the Net Price should reflect the price most consumers can actually pay, with conditions disclosed adjacent to the price rather than only in a general footer.

title: Used vehicle pages do not reference the CARS Act 3-day cancellation right
quote: 41 Used cars, trucks, and SUVs in Stock serving Costa Mesa, Lake Forest & Mission Viejo, CA
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — No used-vehicle page text was captured, so absence cannot be confirmed and no contradictory 'all sales final' language was detected either. The primary 3-day cancellation disclosure is delivered at point of sale, so absence on the website is a best-practice gap rather than a violation. As SB 766 becomes operative Oct 1, 2026, add an accurate reference to the 3-day cancellation right (used vehicles $50,000 or less; restocking fee and mileage limits per statute) on used VLP/VDP pages, and confirm no site terms or arbitration language attempts to waive it.

title: 'Unlock Your Price' CTA may gate pricing behind PI submission without a financial-incentive notice
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — The deterministic crawl flagged has_price_gating=false, but VDPs repeatedly present an 'Unlock Your Price' CTA alongside an already-visible Net/Selling Price, and one homepage lead form (action '/') lacks a privacy link and notice at collection. Could not verify whether 'Unlock Your Price' actually conditions a better price on submitting contact info. If it does, add a notice at collection and a CCPA/CPRA financial-incentive disclosure at the form; if the full price is already shown without submission, no action is needed beyond adding the missing notice-at-collection link to the lead form that lacks it.

title: Unsubstantiated '#1 Rated' superlative ranking claim
quote: #1 Rated Nissan Dealer in O.C....Google Reviews
statute: CA B&P Code 17508 (also Nissan BAP prohibited superlatives)
recommendation: The VDP description and site header use a measurable ranking claim ('#1 Rated Nissan Dealer in O.C.' / "OC's #1 Rated Nissan Dealer on Google"). Although 'Google Reviews' is cited as the basis, a #1 ranking is a factual, verifiable superlative that requires clear substantiation (defined geography, date, and ranking methodology) and may run afoul of Nissan BAP prohibited-superlative rules. Either substantiate the claim with a dated, sourced citation visible to consumers or soften it to non-comparative puffery.
